L0@P0: Chronology and posterity of SGA 5
L1@P0: Luc Illusie
L2@P0: The acronym SGA stands for “Séminaire de Géométrie Algébrique” (“Seminar on Algebraic Geometry”). With the exception of SGA 4 1/2 [17], which
L3@P0: mostly consists1 of texts written by Deligne between 1974 and 1977, it refers
L4@P0: to volumes, numbered from 1 to 7, of a seminar held by Grothendieck at
L5@P0: the Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques (IHÉS) from 1960 through 1969,
L6@P0: published in Lecture Notes in Mathematics nos. 151, 152, 153, 224, 225,
L7@P0: 269, 270, 288, 305, 340, 589 (Springer-Verlag, Berlin-New York); Advanced
L8@P0: Studies in Pure Math. (North Holland), 1968; with partial re-editions in
L9@P0: Documents Mathématiques (SMF) nos. 3, 4, 7, 8. The seminar was labeled
L10@P0: Séminaire de Géométrie Algébrique du Bois-Marie (= “Seminar on Algebraic
L11@P0: Geometry of Bois-Marie”), “Bois-Marie” being the name of the small wood
L12@P0: of the estate in Bures-sur-Yvette, some twenty-eight kilometers south from
L13@P0: Paris, where the IHÉS was located.2
L14@P0: Together with the Éléments de Géométrie Algébrique (= “Elements of Algebraic Geometry”), written with the collaboration of Dieudonné, and published between 1960 and 1967 in Publications Mathématiques de l’IHÉS, 4,
L15@P0: 8, 11, 17, 20, 24, 28, and 32, with a re-edition of EGA 1 in Grundlehren
L16@P0: des mathematischen Wissenschaften 166 (Springer-Verlag, Berlin-New York),
L17@P0: 1971, these seminars introduced and worked out in great detail a new, powerful approach to algebraic geometry, and initiated fundamental, seminal developments. The language and the results of SGA and EGA were to become
L18@P0: universally used by algebraic geometers in the world.
L19@P0: In part I I review the story of SGA 5 from its beginning in 1965 until its
L20@P0: belated publication in 1977. In part II I briefly discuss related developments
L21@P0: that occurred afterwards.
L22@P0: I Chronology of SGA 5
L23@P0: Cohomologie ℓ-adique et fonctions L [30], later3labeled SGA 5, extended
L24@P0: itself over two periods: January 1965 – June 1965, January 1966 – June 1966.
L25@P0: January 1965 – June 1965
L26@P0: 1Deligne’s exposés on étale cohomology [Arcata] were written up by Boutot, [Th. finitude] contains an appendix by Illusie, and [C. D.] is Verdier’s initial text on derived
L27@P0: categories.
L28@P0: 2The first IHÉS buildings opened in 1962. From 1960 to 1962 the seminar was held at
L29@P0: Fondation Thiers, in the 16th arrondissement of Paris.
L30@P0: 3During the course of the oral seminar, the previous seminars had no numbering:
L31@P0: SGA 3 was referred to as SGAD (D for Demazure), and SGA 4 as SGAA (A for Artin).
L32@P0: Grothendieck chose the numbering SGA 1, etc., when SGA 6 started.
L33@P0-1: 1In his first exposés, Grothendieck reviewed the formalism of derived categories, the basic theorems in étale cohomology (proper base change, smooth
L34@P1: base change, ...) and the global duality theorem, which had been established in SGA 4, following the lines of the sketch given by Verdier in [67].
L35@P1: The proof presented in exposés XVII and XVIII of the published version of
L36@P1: SGA 4 [4], which is based on a different approach to the functor f
L37@P1: ! and the
L38@P1: trace morphism, is due to Deligne and was written up by him several years
L39@P1: later.
L40@P1: Then Grothendieck moved on to a part that he considered to make the
L41@P1: real beginning of the seminar, namely, local duality. He introduced the notion of dualizing complexes, discussed their uniqueness and basic properties,
L42@P1: formulated, for the first time, the conjecture of absolute purity, and proved
L43@P1: that modulo this conjecture plus resolution of singularities, on a good regular
L44@P1: scheme X the constant sheaf Z/nZ, for n ∈ Z invertible on X, is dualizing. It
